The test image shows a dead/bleached soybean stem with dark speckling (small black dots/pycnidia) scattered across the surface. The stem is tan/gray with normal white hairs. This pattern strongly suggests a fungal stem disease.

Top candidates: **Phomopsis** (pycnidia on bleached stems) or **Charcoal_Rot** (microsclerotia black dots on stem).

Let me view a Phomopsis reference.

The Phomopsis reference shows seed/pod decay, not matching the stem pattern. However, the test image's core features remain: bleached tan stem with scattered dark speckling (pycnidia) — which is the classic presentation of **Phomopsis stem blight**. The stem is dead/desiccated with small dark fruiting bodies (pycnidia) embedded in the epidermis, exactly as seen in Phomopsis infections on soybean stems.
